role: definition used by deciding rules
quote: **Declaration**—a text recording what the computer should be like: what is installed on it and how it is configured.

role: definition used by deciding rules
quote: The computer is brought into conformity with this text, rather than the text being compiled from the computer.

role: definition used by deciding rules
quote: The declaration consists of files that a person has designated as the primary description of the computer; there may be many files, and together they form one description.

role: definition used by deciding rules
quote: **Installer**—a program of the system whose purpose, according to its documentation, includes installing and removing programs: the system package manager, package managers of programming languages and of application packages.

role: definition used by deciding rules
quote: A general-purpose program with a built-in installer counts as an installer in that part of its functionality.

role: definition used by deciding rules
quote: **Package**—what an installer installs and removes as a whole; in a system that is installed and updated as an image, the image is a package.

role: definition used by deciding rules
quote: **Built-in tool**—a program of the system whose purpose, according to its documentation, includes changing what is installed and settings: an installer, account and rights management, the service manager, network and access rule configuration.

role: definition used by deciding rules
quote: General-purpose programs—an editor, file copying, link creation, the command shell—do not count as built-in tools, except in the part of their functionality that contains a built-in installer.

role: definition used by deciding rules
quote: **In force.** An installed object is in force if it is on the computer; a program, if it runs or can be started.

role: definition used by deciding rules
quote: A setting is in force if it has its value.

role: definition used by deciding rules
quote: A service is in force if it is enabled; an account, if it exists.

role: definition used by deciding rules
quote: The required state of a recorded object is stated by its line.

role: definition used by deciding rules
quote: **Application of the declaration**—an action of the system that brings the computer into conformity with the declaration.

role: definition used by deciding rules
quote: The declaration in force is the declaration of the last application that the system reported as successful [3, Section 3].

role: definition used by deciding rules
quote: **Breaking**—a change to what is installed or settings, made past the declaration through the power of superuser privileges, outside the built-in tools: by writing directly to files, deleting, or disabling system mechanisms.

role: definition used by deciding rules
quote: Breaking is a violation on the person’s part rather than a property of the system, and it refutes no property.

role: deciding rule / scope / order / coverage / clarification
quote: Everything that is installed and every setting must be recorded.

role: deciding rule / scope / order / coverage / clarification
quote: The rest need not be recorded.

role: deciding rule / scope / order / coverage / clarification
quote: The rule applies to objects that are on the computer.

role: deciding rule / scope / order / coverage / clarification
quote: A command that a person typed himself or herself is that person’s action, not an object.

role: deciding rule / scope / order / coverage / clarification
quote: What exists only while the computer runs—a process, an open port, a mount point, a relationship between services—is not considered a separate object: it belongs to the program or setting that creates it, and the decision follows that for the program or setting.

role: deciding rule / scope / order / coverage / clarification
quote: What an object is is determined by four questions asked in order; the first affirmative answer decides, and the clarifications do not change this order.

role: deciding rule / scope / order / coverage / clarification
quote: Is the object a package installed on the computer, or was it obtained as part of such a package and does it remain as received?

role: deciding rule / scope / order / coverage / clarification
quote: Then it is **an installed object**, whether it contains programs or not: fonts, icons, translations, lookup tables, firmware, default setting values, a package containing only dependencies.

role: deciding rule / scope / order / coverage / clarification
quote: Is the object code that the computer executes or can execute: on its own, at a person’s command, or through another program with that program’s rights?

role: deciding rule / scope / order / coverage / clarification
quote: Then it is a **program**, whoever wrote it and wherever it came from; a program belongs to what is installed.

role: deciding rule / scope / order / coverage / clarification
quote: Is the object a value chosen by a person that the computer as a whole obeys, rather than only a program that a person runs for himself or herself?

role: deciding rule / scope / order / coverage / clarification
quote: Then it is a **setting**, however it was entered and whatever file stores it.

role: deciding rule / scope / order / coverage / clarification
quote: Settings are services and their parameters, the network, including saved networks, devices and filesystems, time and language, accounts, rights, access rules and what is permitted as a means of login to this computer.

role: deciding rule / scope / order / coverage / clarification
quote: A value obeyed only by a program that a person runs for himself or herself is a setting if it launches something or grants access; otherwise it is a record of that program.

role: deciding rule / scope / order / coverage / clarification
quote: Otherwise: if a program recorded the object as it ran, it is a **program record**—a log, cache, history, working state; if a person created or brought the object, it is **material**—documents, photographs, projects, downloaded files, private keys and passwords for logging in to other machines.

role: deciding rule / scope / order / coverage / clarification
quote: What is installed is recorded by one of three lines: a line of its own; the line of the package as part of which it was obtained; a line from which the system itself built or obtained it—a compiled copy, a generated list, a package installed as a dependency of a recorded package.

role: deciding rule / scope / order / coverage / clarification
quote: A setting is recorded by a line of its own; a default value obtained with a package or created during its installation is covered by the line of the package.

role: deciding rule / scope / order / coverage / clarification
quote: A line may take a list from outside the declaration, for example accounts from an organisation’s server; in that case, what counts as recorded is the source named in the line.

role: deciding rule / scope / order / coverage / clarification
quote: What need not be recorded may also be recorded in the declaration.

role: deciding rule / scope / order / coverage / clarification
quote: A file containing code that cannot be executed on this computer is not a program.

role: deciding rule / scope / order / coverage / clarification
quote: Code that runs inside a recorded program and cannot itself launch programs or change what is installed and the computer’s settings—a web page in a browser, a guest system in a virtual machine—need not be recorded.

role: deciding rule / scope / order / coverage / clarification
quote: A program that runs as its own process on the computer, including in a container, is a program.

role: deciding rule / scope / order / coverage / clarification
quote: A file that a program executes as code counts as code even when it contains setting values; a file that a program only reads as values does not count as code.
